newsitem.title: UK: Oil slides as gasoline season ends, Iraq looms.
newsitem.headline: Oil slides as gasoline season ends, Iraq looms.

text.p: Oil prices eased on Thursday as Iraq took another step towards resuming crude exports under the terms of a United Nations humanitarian plan and traders began to focus on ample supplies of heating fuel.
Bellwether Brent blend crude oil for August delivery shed 44 cents to trade at $18.48 a barrel on Thursday, ending a run of four days of successive gains.
Recent strength has come from uncertainty about the timing of the resumption of Iraqi exports -- suspended since late May -- and seasonal demand for gasoline.

But with New York markets winding down for the July 4 Independence Day holiday, which traditionally marks the peak of gasoline demand as millions of U.S. motorists head for the beach or holiday homes, traders said crude prices would lose a key prop.
"Interest should therefore be shifting slowly towards the distillate markets but these seem sadly over supplied at present, keeping prices down," said brokers MeesPierson.

Stocks of diesel and heating fuel in the United States, the world's biggest oil importer, rose by a hefty four million barrels last week to stand nearly 17 million barrels above year-ago levels, according to data released by the American Petroleum Institute (API).

Distillates inventories usually rise during the northern hemisphere summer when demand for heating oil is at a minimum but dealers say a disappointing gasoline season has prompted refineries to start stockpiling ahead of time.
"The gasoline season never really kicked off and distillates are now looking very bearish," said a broker.
News that Iraq and the United Nations have completed their food distribution plan to cover the proceeds of the next six months of oil exports helped remove another crutch from world crude markets.

Iraq's U.N. coordinator Staffan de Mistura said Baghdad authorities had told him their plan for distributing aid in the centre and south of the country was ready but needed some "fine tuning" before it could be presented to the U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
"We are in process of finalising the distribution plan which according to the government is crucial in order to decide on the renewal of oil sales," de Mistura told Reuters.
Iraqi exports during the first six months of the oil-for-food deal, implemented last December, average nearly 660,000 barrels per day (bpd) or equivalent to the daily output of OPEC minnow Qatar.
The accord's renewal took effect on June 8 but Baghdad delayed restarting exports because it was unhappy with the cumbersome plan for distributing food and medicine.
Oil refineries, particularly in southern Europe, have been left srabbling around for alternative feedstocks, pushing crude markets higher.
OPEC kingpin Saudi Arabia on Wednesday took advantage of spot market strength to raise its term contract prices for August by between 10 and 55 cents a barrel for western hemisphere customers.
